:::{#thm-expected-probability-collision}
#### The expected probability is the collision probability

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
and let $X'$ be a variable such that $X$ and $X'$ are [IID](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-iid).
Then

$$\E{\P(X)} = \sum_x \P(X=x)^2 = \P(X = X').$$

:::

::: proof

The [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of $\P(X)$ adds, over the values $x$,
the value $\P(X=x)$ times its [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $\P(X=x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\P(X)}
&= \sum_x \P(X=x) \, \P(X=x) \\
&= \sum_x \P(X=x)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The variables $X$ and $X'$ take the same value exactly when both equal some value $x$.
Because $X$ and $X'$ are IID,
the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) that both equal $x$ is $\P(X=x) \, \P(X'=x) = \P(X=x)^2$.
Adding over the values $x$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\P(X = X')
&= \sum_x \P(X=x, X'=x) \\
&= \sum_x \P(X=x)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

By the definition of the [collision probability](#def-collision-probability),
this is the collision probability.

:::
